The best free to-do list apps

The big to-do apps are all free to start, with limits on lists, reminders or views that lift when you pay. Here is what each free version does, from its own pages, and which one suits whom.

We make Slop To-do, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • What the free version allows: lists, tasks, reminders
  • Due dates, repeats, subtasks, tags and views
  • Apps on every device, sync and sharing
  • Account needed, and where your tasks are kept

1. Microsoft To Do

Best for: A completely free to-do app on every device, with shared lists and Outlook tasks

Good

  • Free on the web, iOS, Mac, Android and Windows, as its store listing says
  • My Day planner, steps, notes, files up to 25 MB, repeating due dates and reminders
  • Shared lists; syncs with Outlook tasks and flagged emails

Not so good

  • Lists and tasks are hosted on Microsoft 365, not kept only on your device
  • No board or calendar view mentioned on its pages

Microsoft To Do website · Sources: Microsoft To Do on Google Play, Microsoft To Do on the App Store, Microsoft Support: due dates and reminders

2. Todoist (Beginner)

Best for: Fast task capture with labels, filters and a board view, for personal use

Good

  • Due dates and times, priorities, sub-tasks, reminders, labels and repeating dates free
  • List and board layouts; comments and assigned tasks
  • 90+ integrations

Not so good

  • Five personal projects on the free plan
  • Calendar layout, custom reminders, task duration and automatic backups are on Pro
  • One week of activity history

Todoist (Beginner) website · Sources: Todoist pricing and plan table

3. TickTick (Free)

Best for: Tasks, habits and a basic calendar in one app, within small limits

Good

  • List and Kanban views, a basic calendar and an Eisenhower matrix free
  • Subtasks, tags, priorities, repeating tasks and templates
  • Habits and countdowns (5 each) and cross-platform sync

Not so good

  • Free limits: 9 lists, 99 tasks per list, 19 checklist items per task
  • Duration, filters, timeline view and constant reminders are Premium
  • One attachment a day

TickTick (Free) website · Sources: TickTick pricing and comparison

4. Slop To-do (ours)

Best for: A private list on one device with no limits and no sign-up, shown in Slop Calendar

Tasks with due dates and times in a time zone, priorities, lists, tags, one level of subtasks, repeats and reminders, with Today, Upcoming and All views; tasks with a time appear in Slop Calendar.

Good

  • No account, no limits on lists or tasks, nothing uploaded
  • Due times in any time zone, repeats (daily to yearly, with an end day) and reminders
  • Tasks with a time show in Slop Calendar; completing in either app updates both

Not so good

  • No sync between devices and no sharing
  • Reminders only pop up while Slop To-do, Calendar or Reminders is open (or as a browser notification you allow)
  • No board view, no file attachments; subtasks one level deep

Open Slop To-do

Which one to choose

If you want one free app on your phone and computer, Microsoft To Do is the most generous: free everywhere, with sharing and Outlook integration. Todoist and TickTick have more views and power features, but their free plans cap projects or lists.

Slop To-do is for a private list on one device with no sign-up and no limits, linked to Slop Calendar. It does not sync or share, so it is not the one for a household or a team.

Questions

What is the best free to-do list app?

Microsoft To Do is free on every platform with shared lists. Todoist (five projects) and TickTick (nine lists) have strong free plans with limits. Slop To-do has no limits but stays on one device.

Which to-do app is free without limits?

Slop To-do sets no limits. Microsoft To Do's pages describe it as free and state no list limits. Todoist and TickTick limit projects or lists on their free plans.

Can I use a to-do list without an account?

Slop To-do works with no account and keeps tasks in your browser. Todoist and TickTick need an account; Microsoft To Do hosts lists on Microsoft 365.

Which free to-do app syncs between phone and computer?

Microsoft To Do and TickTick say they sync across devices. Slop To-do does not sync; each browser keeps its own list.
